newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates hold in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates hold in brisk trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates held in brisk morning trade on Monday as banks sought fresh kuna funds, dealers said.
"Today was marked by demand for reserve payment and for last week's foreign exchange deals with the central bank," said dealer Jasenka Blagaic.
On Thursday, the central bank sold commercial banks 7.5 million German marks ($4.6 million) and $4.5 million, which have payments due today.
Some borrowers who could not repay overnight loans also asked for them to be rolled over.
Blagaic said 56 million kuna ($9.8 million) in fresh demand was almost entirely met, with two savings banks left empty-handed.
Most new borrowings were interbank call money loans at a steady 10.5 percent, with one at 11 percent.

Overnight trade over the weekend totalled 26.6 million kuna after Friday's tax payment drained most banks' accounts and some borrowed money to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
